title: Message Adapter Gateway: OpenAI ChatCompletions request/response mapping and streaming semantics
creator: Ravi Singh
description:
Problem: Customers integrating older OpenAI Chat Completions clients send/expect a variety of request shapes (message arrays, role/name variants, top-level parameters like stop/temperature) and streaming pieces delivered as SSE 'delta' chunks. Our Redwood API uses a different internal request/response model (structured tool_call objects, unified streaming frames, and token-level telemetry). We need an adapter gateway that reliably maps incoming OpenAI ChatCompletions requests to Redwood's internal shape and maps responses back so existing clients experience minimal behavior change.

Scope: implement a stateless gateway layer in the public API edge that performs: request shaping (role/name normalization, legacy 'messages' -> internal prompt blocks, legacy top-level params -> route config), streaming framing translation (server-sent events vs Redwood streaming frames), function/tool call representation mapping (OpenAI's function_call proposal -> Redwood tool_call.model / tooling), error and status mapping, and conservative defaulting for ambiguous fields. The adapter must preserve observability headers and attach metadata for billing and model selection.

Why now: Increased customer requests for OpenAI-compat endpoints and multiple support tickets where client-side SDKs break when we introduce structured tool outputs. This is a medium-term requirement to reduce migration friction while we encourage adoption of Redwood-native SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming ChatCompletions /v1/chat/completions requests accepted with message arrays and legacy params are correctly translated to Redwood internal request format
Streaming responses to OpenAI clients use SSE framing with 'delta' events preserving chunk order and finalization signals (role/name/function_call)
Function/tool calls are surfaced to clients using shape compatible with OpenAI's function_call field while still recording Redwood tool_call telemetry internally
Edge adapter includes tests (unit + integration) that cover at least 90% of mapping rules in the schema compat matrix
No regressions in latency p50/p95 beyond 5ms introduced at edge path in our performance test harness
Migration docs and example SDK snippets published and linked from console docs
design_notes: We implement a thin translator at the API gateway: 1) Request normalization: canonicalize roles (system/user/assistant), map legacy 'name' and 'role' variants, hoist top-level params (temperature/stop/max_tokens) into internal route config; detect 'messages' with mixed content (strings vs JSON) and coerce to internal blocks. 2) Streaming: subscribe to Redwood streaming frames and re-emit as SSE lines with event: 'delta' and event: 'done' semantics. Include 'index' sequence numbers to help clients reassemble out-of-order frames. 3) Function/tool calling: map Redwood structured tool_call {tool:...,args:...,structured:...} into OpenAI-compatible {name,arguments} stringified JSON in 'function_call' payloads while keeping an internal mapping id so responses can be reconciled when clients supply tool results. 4) Errors: convert internal error codes into OpenAI-like HTTP 4xx/5xx top-level error object with 'type' and 'message'. 5) Telemetry: propagate request-id, user-id, and add header 'X-Compat-Adapter: openai-chat-2026-03' for internal traces.
decisions: Prefer non-destructive mapping: when ambiguous, include both forms (e.g., preserve original messages array in metadata) rather than dropping fields
Emit SSE style streaming for OpenAI clients because many SDKs expect event: 'delta' chunks
Keep adapter stateless so it can be horizontally scaled and retired once clients migrate
tradeoffs: We will accept minor increase in edge CPU due to per-request JSON mapping logic to reduce customer migration work. This is simpler and lower-risk than forcing immediate SDK changes. However, keeping mapping logic at edge duplicates some validation logic and will require synchronization with runtime changes (e.g., new structured output fields).
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Build request normalizer module with full test suite (unit + schema fuzz tests)
Phase 2: Integrate streaming frame translator and add end-to-end tests with a mock OpenAI client
Phase 3: Implement function/tool_call mapping and reconciliation hooks; add telemetry mapping
Phase 4: Run internal canary against low-traffic domain and measure latency/percentile regressions
Phase 5: Docs, migration guides, and public announcement
testing_plan: Unit tests for 40+ mapping rules from compatibility matrix
Integration tests: replay 10k recorded OpenAI requests through the gateway in staging
Load test: 10k concurrent SSE clients to ensure streaming pipeline backpressure behaves
Behavioral tests: ensure tool_call roundtrip works when client supplies external tool results
Telemetry tests: ensure X-Compat-Adapter header present and request-id preserved
rollout_strategy: Canary 1% of traffic (non-SLA customers) for 72 hours
Promote to 10% after stability checks and perf thresholds are met
Monitor: latency p50/p95, error rate, telemetry mapping accuracy, customer support queue
Fallback: routing rule to bypass adapter and serve native internal path if error spikes
